about:
MicroLink Devices was founded in 2000 in Niles, Illinois, a northern suburb of Chicago. The company operates a 30,000-square-foot facility that houses a clean room, device fabrication and test laboratories, and a full suite of metalorganic chemical vapor deposition (MOCVD) tools for high-volume epitaxial growth. Ownership details and founder names are not publicly disclosed.

The company designs and manufactures III-V epitaxial materials for wireless communications, including cellular phones, and produces high-efficiency single- and multi-junction gallium arsenide (GaAs) solar cells and sheets for unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), spacecraft, and terrestrial collectors. Its proprietary epitaxial lift-off (ELO) process separates the solar cell structure from the growth substrate, yielding lightweight, flexible cells while allowing the substrate to be reused multiple times. MicroLink owns all equipment needed for growth, fabrication, and testing of epitaxial materials and solar devices.

MicroLink serves the aerospace, defense, and renewable energy sectors. Since 2003 it has been a prime federal contractor on more than thirty programs developing solar cells, transistors, and lasers. Its customer base includes government agencies and commercial firms seeking custom epitaxial materials, solar sheets for UAVs and satellites, and contract research and development support.

The company emphasizes quality and technical depth: it is ISO 9001 certified, employs staff recognized as experts in GaAs- and InP-based device growth and processing, and supports customers through both development and production phases to improve yield and performance. The ELO technology, developed through its federal R&D programs, is cited as a key differentiator that reduces cost and enables flexible, high-specific-power solar solutions.
